ai.literal: Arrogance, anger, and meanness, those who are without; [their] prosperity is of a majestic nature.
ai.translation: The prosperity of those who are free from arrogance, anger, and meanness possesses true majesty.
ai.modern: செருக்கு, சினம், சிறுமை ஆகிய மூன்று குற்றங்களும் இல்லாதவர்களின் செல்வமும் சிறப்பும் பெருமைக்குரிய தன்மையைக் கொண்டிருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet identifies three major flaws that destroy a person's greatness: arrogance, anger, and petty meanness. It states that only when an individual is completely free from these three faults does their wealth or power attain true dignity. The word 'பெருக்கம்' denotes material or social prosperity, while 'பெருமித நீர்த்து' elevates it to a majestic, honorable state.

ai.literal: Miserliness and, excellence lost pride and, unbecoming joy and, (are) faults to a king.
ai.translation: Miserliness, pride devoid of dignity, and unbecoming joy are flaws in a ruler.
ai.modern: கஞ்சத்தனம், பெருமை இல்லாத வீண் மானம், தகுதியற்ற மகிழ்ச்சி ஆகிய மூன்றும் ஒரு தலைவனுக்குக் குற்றங்களாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet identifies three specific flaws that a ruler must eradicate. The first is ivaṟal, which means extreme miserliness or greed that prevents proper generosity. The second is māṇpu iṟanta mānam, a false pride or arrogance that has lost true dignity and excellence. The third is māṇā uvakai, an unbecoming or inappropriate joy, such as gloating or indulging in petty pleasures. Together, these three traits are declared as ētam (faults or harms) that will ruin a leader.

ai.literal: Millet-measure-becoming fault even-if-comes palm-measure-as they-will-consider blame those-who-fear.
ai.translation: Those who shrink from disgrace will consider a fault as big as a palm tree, even if it is only the size of a millet seed.
ai.modern: பழிக்கு அஞ்சுகின்றவர்கள், தினை அளவு சிறிய குற்றம் வந்தாலும், அதனைப் பனை அளவு பெரியதாகக் கருதுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the tiny millet seed with the massive palmyra tree to illustrate how the virtuous view their own mistakes. Those who deeply fear disgrace do not dismiss small errors. Instead, they magnify even the slightest fault to ensure they maintain their moral integrity.

ai.literal: Fault-indeed let one guard against as the main objective; fault-indeed is the ruin bringing enemy.
ai.translation: Make guarding against faults your primary objective, for a fault is an enemy that brings about your ruin.
ai.modern: குற்றம் ஏற்படாமல் காத்துக்கொள்வதையே ஒருவன் தன் முக்கிய நோக்கமாகக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்; ஏனெனில், குற்றமே ஒருவனுக்கு அழிவைத் தரும் பகையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises making the avoidance of faults one's primary goal in life. The word 'பொருளாக' (as the main objective or wealth) emphasizes that guarding against one's own flaws is as important as acquiring wealth. The repetition of 'குற்றமே' (fault itself) stresses that one's own mistakes are the real danger. Ultimately, a fault acts as an internal enemy that brings about one's downfall.

ai.literal: Before coming, he who guards not, life, before fire, straw stack like, will perish.
ai.translation: The life of one who does not guard against a fault before it happens will perish like a haystack placed before a fire.
ai.modern: குற்றம் வருவதற்கு முன்பே அதைக் காத்துக்கொள்ளாதவனுடைய வாழ்க்கை, நெருப்பின் முன்னால் வைக்கப்பட்ட வைக்கோல் போர் எரிந்து அழிவதைப் போல அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the danger of not anticipating and preventing faults. The phrase 'varu muṉṉar' (before it comes) emphasizes the need for foresight and proactive defense against errors. The word 'vai' means straw and 'tūṟu' means a stack or heap; together they form a haystack. Just as a dry haystack is instantly consumed when placed in front of a fire, the life and prosperity of a person who fails to guard against impending faults will be swiftly and completely destroyed.

ai.literal: One's own fault having removed, others' fault if able to see, what fault will happen to the king?
ai.translation: If a leader first removes his own faults and then looks into the faults of others, what fault can ever befall him?
ai.modern: தன் குற்றத்தை முதலில் நீக்கிவிட்டு, அதன் பிறகு மற்றவர்களின் குற்றத்தை ஆராயும் தலைவனுக்கு என்ன குற்றம் நேரிடும்?
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of self-correction for a leader. The word இறை refers to a king or leader. The phrase காண்கிற்பின் implies not just seeing, but having the moral authority and ability to examine others' flaws. By removing one's own faults first, a leader becomes immune to reproach, and no fault can attach to them.

ai.literal: Things that should be done - without doing - of the miser - wealth - that which has the nature of surviving - without being - will perish.
ai.translation: The wealth of a miser who hoards without doing what ought to be done will perish, having no chance of survival.
ai.modern: செய்ய வேண்டிய நற்செயல்களைச் செய்யாமல் பொருளைச் சேர்த்து வைக்கும் கஞ்சனுடைய செல்வம், தப்பிப் பிழைக்கும் தன்மை இல்லாமல் அழிந்து போகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the vice of miserliness and the failure to perform one's duties. The word 'செயற்பால' refers to the necessary good deeds, such as charity or supporting one's dependents, for which wealth is meant. When a person hoards wealth ('இவறியான்') without fulfilling these obligations, that wealth is doomed. The phrase 'உயற்பாலது அன்றி' emphasizes that such hoarded wealth has absolutely no means of survival and will inevitably be lost.

ai.literal: The miserly mind which is called miserliness, among anything, to be considered that which is one thing it is not.
ai.translation: The grasping mindset known as miserliness is not a thing to be counted among any category of worthy traits.
ai.modern: பற்றுள்ளம் என்று சொல்லப்படும் கஞ்சத்தனம், எந்தப் பொருள்களின் கூட்டத்திலும் சேர்த்து எண்ணப்படும் தகுதி உடையது அல்ல.
ai.explanation: This couplet condemns the extreme greed that prevents a person from sharing their wealth. The word 'பற்றுள்ளம்' describes a mind that tightly grasps onto things without ever letting go. The poet states that such a miserly nature is so base that it cannot even be classified or counted among any recognized human traits. It is a complete negation of human worth.

ai.literal: Let not praise at any time oneself; let not desire good not yielding action.
ai.translation: Never praise yourself at any time, and never desire to do deeds that yield no good.
ai.modern: எந்தக் காலத்திலும் தன்னைத் தானே புகழ்ந்து கொள்ளக் கூடாது; நன்மை தராத செயல்களைச் செய்ய விரும்பவும் கூடாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises against two major faults: self-praise and engaging in useless deeds. The word 'வியவற்க' means 'do not marvel at or praise', warning a person never to boast about themselves ('தன்னை') at any time ('எஞ்ஞான்றும்'). Furthermore, 'நயவற்க' means 'do not desire', instructing them to avoid any action ('வினை') that does not yield ('பயவா') a good outcome ('நன்றி'). By avoiding arrogance and fruitless actions, one maintains clear judgment and effectiveness.

ai.literal: Desired things, attachment without knowing if one can manage, useless [are] enemies' designs.
ai.translation: If a ruler can manage his desires so that his attachments remain unknown, the strategies of his enemies will be rendered useless.
ai.modern: தான் விரும்பும் பொருள்களின் மீதான ஆசையை மற்றவர் அறியாதபடி ஒருவனால் அனுபவிக்க முடியுமானால், பகைவரின் சூழ்ச்சிகள் அவனிடம் பலிக்காமல் வீணாகிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises leaders on the importance of concealing their personal desires and attachments. The word 'காதல' refers to the things one desires, while 'காதல் அறியாமை' means keeping the extent of that desire hidden from others. If a leader can manage ('உய்க்கிற்பின்') this discretion, the 'நூல்' (which usually means books or threads, but here means calculated strategies) of enemies will become 'ஏதில' (useless), because enemies cannot exploit weaknesses they cannot see.
